text: Mahler coefficient equivariance follows directly from the finite-difference formula in [Colmez I.2.2–I.2.3](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=8). The displayed hypotheses correctly require a continuous additive scalar action; commutation with the ℤ_p action is unnecessary for this forward coefficient identity. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean#L73).

The exposed value preserves Mathlib’s forward map, inverse and norm. Its S-linearity is proved by finite differences, so this is precisely the scalar refinement of [Colmez’s Mahler isometry, I.2.3](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~pierre.colmez/fonctionsdunevariable.pdf#page=8), with the broader module hypotheses justified in Lean. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean#L82).
The scalar-refined equivalence has exactly the original forward Mahler coefficient map.
The scalar-refined inverse remains exactly the original Mahler series map.

The exposed Pi.single value is the ordinary coordinate vector of [Serre’s c(I), §1](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=3). The same/other-coordinate equations and zero case agree; finite support ensures decay for the stated general topological codomain. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/Discrete.lean#L119).
The selected coordinate of single i b is b.
Every other coordinate of single i b is zero.
A zero entry gives the zero coordinate vector.

The upper bound is coordinatewise, and evaluation at i gives the reverse bound. This is the coordinate sup-norm convention of [Serre §1](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=3), valid also for a seminorm and for a zero entry. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/Discrete.lean#L197).
The selected coordinate of single i b is b.
A zero entry gives the zero coordinate vector.

Finite partial sums retain exactly the selected coordinates, so their error has arbitrarily small sup norm by cofinite decay. This verifies the coordinate expansion underlying [Serre §1–2](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4), including arbitrary index sets without a completeness assumption. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/Discrete.lean#L228).
A finite coordinate sum keeps precisely the entries in its summation set.

The coordinate expansion determines each continuous linear map, as in [Serre’s coordinate argument, §2](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4). Testing every single i b handles module-valued coordinates correctly; T2Space M supplies the needed uniqueness of limits. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/Discrete.lean#L243).
Finite coordinate partial sums converge in the source sup seminorm to the given family.

Each term is bounded by ‖a‖‖e‖, and the ultrametric sum bound yields the claim. Unlike the convergent construction in [Serre §2](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4), this helper permits nonsummability: Lean’s default tsum is then zero. Its name and docstring assert only the valid norm inequality. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L86).

The estimate ‖a_i·e_i‖≤‖a_i‖‖e‖ gives precisely cofinite decay. This is the convergence input for [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4); the Lean helper correctly needs neither completeness nor ultrametricity. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L98).
On a discrete index, vanishing at infinity is decay along the cofinite filter.

The terms decay by the preceding estimate, and completeness plus ultrametricity turns that decay into unconditional summability. These are the convergence assumptions behind [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4); no countability restriction is inserted. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L109).
Null coefficients paired with a bounded family give terms tending to zero along the cofinite filter.

The exposed value is the convergent sum a↦Σ a_i·e_i, with continuity supplied by ‖e‖. It matches the construction in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4). The weaker ring hypotheses are sound: convergence occurs in M, and no converse boundedness claim is made. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L116).
The extension map is the genuine unconditional sum of the stated terms.
The extension sends single i r to r acting on the i-th family member.

This is the defining equality for the construction in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4). The summability hypotheses are retained, so the displayed sum is genuine; argument order and the left scalar action agree with the definition. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L130).
The extension map is the genuine unconditional sum of the stated terms.

Only the i-th summand survives, giving r·e_i and, at r=1, the prescribed family member. This is exactly the coordinate characterization used in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4); noncommutative scalar order is preserved. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L141).
The selected coordinate of single i b is b.
Every other coordinate of single i b is zero.

The map’s defining sum has norm at most ‖e‖‖a‖ by the ultrametric inequality. This verifies the extension estimate in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4); contractive scalar multiplication supplies exactly this constant. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L160).
The ultrametric pairing estimate has the exact product of the two sup norms as its bound.

The explicit pointwise bound puts ‖e‖ in the set defining the scoped ring operator norm. This is the upper half of [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4), and remains valid without Tate scalars because this particular map is already bounded. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L165).
The constructed operator has the explicit uniform bound given by the family norm.

The upper bound is established, while testing single i 1 gives every ‖e_i‖ as a lower bound. The explicit NormOneClass assumption makes those test vectors unit norm. Thus the norm equality in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4) extends correctly to these rings, including empty I. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L170).
The extension sends single i r to r acting on the i-th family member.
A single coordinate vector has exactly the norm of its entry.

Both maps take single i r to r·e_i+r·f_i, so coordinate extensionality gives equality. This is the additive part of the correspondence in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4); it requires no commutativity of R. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L187).
The extension sends single i r to r acting on the i-th family member.

The uniform bound for Tate-linear maps applies to single i 1, giving bounded coordinate images. This verifies the inverse-direction input in [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4). The Tate hypothesis is retained; no unjustified implication from continuity over arbitrary rings is used. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L219).
Under Tate scalars, continuity implies an actual finite uniform operator bound.
A single coordinate vector has exactly the norm of its entry.

The reconstructed map agrees with u on single i r because single i r=r·single i 1. Coordinate extensionality then recovers u, exactly the inverse argument of [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4), with Tate boundedness explicitly supplied. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L229).
The extension sends single i r to r acting on the i-th family member.
Agreement on all coordinate vectors identifies continuous linear maps.

On single i r, both sides agree by commuting c with r. The explicit commutative-ring hypothesis therefore justifies the scalar-linearity component of [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4); no Tate condition is needed for this forward identity. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L250).
The extension sends single i r to r acting on the i-th family member.

The exposed maps are bounded-family extension and evaluation on unit coordinates. Their inverse laws and norm equality give the correspondence of [Serre §2, Proposition 3](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1962__12__69_0.pdf#page=4). Tate scalars supply the necessary global bound, and commutativity supplies the operator-space scalar action. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty/LinearCombination.lean#L279).
The forward equivalence is the linear combination construction.
The inverse equivalence evaluates the operator on each unit coordinate vector.
The constructed operator norm equals the bounded-family sup norm under the stated norm-one hypothesis.

The ordinary kernel is two-sided; counit compatibility gives ε(x)=0 and antipode compatibility gives f(Sx)=S(fx)=0. The remaining comultiplication condition is explicitly assumed, matching [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78). Thus the semiring construction does not claim that every kernel is automatically a coideal. Published [membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L96) and [surjective-specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L139) controls pass.
Conditional kernel has exactly the zero fiber, with hcomul retained.
Surjective specialization retains the ordinary kernel carrier.

Forgetting the Hopf conditions returns exactly RingHom.ker f. This is the ideal of elements mapped to zero, consistent with [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78) adding conditions to an existing ideal. The rendered hcomul argument retains its complete tensor-sum condition. The published [membership calculation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L96) passes; no ideal generation, radical, or quotient replacement occurs.
Conditional kernel has exactly the zero fiber, with hcomul retained.

Membership is precisely f(x)=0 in the codomain, obtained from the unchanged ring-hom kernel. The Hopf laws of [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78) add no further elementwise test. The published [surjective specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L145) passes. In particular this says nothing about equality of arbitrary fibers over semirings; the separate zero-kernel/injectivity theorem correctly strengthens the domain to a ring.
Surjective Hopf-kernel membership is f(x)=0.

When H is a ring, f(x)=f(y) is equivalent to f(x−y)=0; hence a zero kernel is equivalent to injectivity. This agrees with the mechanism behind [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The explicit Ring H hypothesis is essential to this argument and is present in the rendered statement. The published [surjective specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L151) passes; surjectivity and flatness are unnecessary once hcomul is supplied.
Ring-domain zero-kernel/injectivity equivalence.

Surjectivity identifies ker(f⊗f) with the sum of the two tensor-kernel images by [tensor right exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). Comultiplication compatibility then supplies the missing Hopf-ideal law in [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78). The published [quotient recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L282) and [counit-kernel example](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Augmentation.lean#L113) pass. No flatness, commutativity of H, reducedness, or invertible antipode is assumed.
Actual quotient map recovers its defining Hopf ideal without flatness.
Actual split-surjective counit example has its ordinary counit kernel.

The bundled surjective kernel has exactly the ordinary ideal kernel. This matches [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35) and the ideal-based convention in [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78). The published [augmentation formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Augmentation.lean#L113) passes for the surjective counit. The conclusion is equality of ideals, so subsequent quotient constructions use the original kernel rather than an enlargement chosen to enforce Hopf closure.
Actual split-surjective counit example has its ordinary counit kernel.

An element is in this Hopf ideal exactly when its image is zero. The result applies the ordinary ideal-kernel convention used by [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The published [augmentation membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Augmentation.lean#L73) and [quotient recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L282) pass, checking both counit and quotient-map specializations. Surjectivity constructs the Hopf structure; it does not alter kernel membership.
Actual augmentation example is precisely vanishing of the counit.
Actual quotient map recovers its defining Hopf ideal without flatness.

The ordinary kernel criterion underlying [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35) gives injectivity exactly when the bundled kernel is zero. The ring hypotheses support subtraction, and hf supplies the Hopf kernel. The published [image/preimage recovery for bijections](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Map.lean#L326) passes and uses this criterion to remove the kernel summand. The statement does not assert that surjectivity alone implies a zero kernel.
Published bijection consumer removes the kernel summand using zero-kernel criterion.

The displayed assumptions require both K and H/ker(f) to be flat over R. Factoring f through its injective kernel quotient then makes the tensor square injective, using [Stacks, flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9); this yields the coideal condition in [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78). The published [comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L191) and [flat quotient recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L205) pass. Over a field these flatness assumptions hold automatically; arbitrary base rings still retain them.
Surjective and flat constructions agree when both sets of hypotheses hold.
Flat-kernel quotient recovery explicitly retains flatness of H/I.

This forgetful identity retains the ordinary kernel, rather than choosing a different ideal with a flat quotient. Both flatness assumptions are already hypotheses of the displayed constructor, in the sense of [Stacks, flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). The published [membership theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L176) passes and confirms the same zero fiber. The statement does not infer flatness for arbitrary kernel quotients.
Flat kernel membership is f(x)=0, with both flatness hypotheses.

The flat kernel construction still consists exactly of elements sent to zero, as in [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Its flatness assumptions justify the Hopf structure and do not change that carrier. The published [postcomposition inclusion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L182) and [quotient recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L205) pass. The latter retains the flatness of the quotient required by this particular kernel constructor.
Postcomposition inclusion follows elementwise from the same zero fiber.
Flat-kernel quotient recovery explicitly retains flatness of H/I.

If f(x)=0 then g(f(x))=0, so ker(f)⊆ker(g∘f). The composition order and inclusion direction are correct. All four flatness instances needed to construct the two Hopf kernels are displayed; their meaning is [Stacks, flatness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). The published [normal-product containment](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Normal/Product/Properties.lean#L125) passes as an actual field-level consumer. Equality is not claimed when g can kill additional elements.
Published field-level normal-product containment applies ker_le_ker_comp and quotient recovery.

Both constructions have the same ordinary kernel and differ only in proofs of its Hopf laws. Extensionality therefore identifies them whenever surjectivity and both flatness hypotheses hold. This is consistent with [Kytölä’s Hopf-ideal definition](https://math.aalto.fi/~kkytola/files_KK/lectures_files_KK/Hopf-lecture_notes.pdf#page=78) treating the laws as properties of an ideal. The published [surjective carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L139) and [flat carrier](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L170) controls pass. The theorem does not claim that surjectivity alone forces a flat codomain.
Surjective specialization retains the ordinary kernel carrier.
Flat kernel retains the ordinary ideal kernel.

The map sends [h] to f(h), the same forward map as [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35), upgraded to preserve comultiplication and counit through the quotient universal property. The published [representative formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L226) and [factorization identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L233) pass. Its domain is H/ker(f) and its codomain is K; surjectivity supplies the kernel Hopf structure, with no flatness premise.
Published quotient-class evaluation: the lift sends [h] to f(h).
Published factorization as equality of bialgebra morphisms.

The kernel quotient lift evaluates on [h] as f(h), agreeing with [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). The equality is independent of representative because f kills exactly the quotient ideal. The published [bijectivity proof](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L241) passes and uses this formula for both directions. The statement returns an element of K and does not choose a preimage in H.
Actual proof uses quotient-class evaluation in both injectivity and surjectivity.

This is the factorization f= f̄∘q with q:H→H/ker(f), in the same direction as [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35). Equality is of bialgebra morphisms, so the algebra and coalgebra structures are preserved together. The published [pointwise quotient-class formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L226) passes. The composite is defined on H; the statement makes no claim that q∘f̄ is meaningful or equals an identity.
Published quotient-class evaluation: the lift sends [h] to f(h).

Injectivity follows from f(h)=0 iff h lies in the quotient ideal; surjectivity follows by choosing h with f(h)=k. This is the first-isomorphism mechanism of [Mathlib’s kernel quotient](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L35).
